sections.label: Budget cut for Parliament debate
sections.summary: The Chairman moves to reduce Head F of the Estimates by $100, with the cut concerning Parliament as an effective and respected political arena.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head F of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Chairman, my cut is about how to ensure that our Parliament will always be an effective and respected political arena.

sections.label: Divisive issues in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore will have to continue dealing with divisive issues such as wealth, foreigners, race and religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we will have to continue to deal with all sorts of divisive issues, such as on wealth, foreigners, as well as race and religion.

sections.label: Four principles for parliamentary debate
sections.summary: Four principles are proposed to guide parliamentary debate: being factually accurate, highlighting benefits and trade-offs, being constructive, and avoiding polarisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can promote critical thinking among our populace, but not cynicism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would thus like to propose four principles to guide how issues should be brought up and debated within our Parliament: one, being factually accurate; two, highlight both benefits and trade-offs; three, being constructive; and four, avoid creating polarisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the Singapore Parliament will always remain functional and respected by our people.

sections.label: Lying and half-truths in Parliament
sections.summary: Lying in Parliament erodes trust and debilitates democracy, and half-truths, misleading statements and innuendos must also be guarded against.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Lying in Parliament, or to any Committee of Parliament, erodes trust and debilitates our democracy.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: What is less obvious, but equally dangerous and which we must also guard against, are half-truths, misleading statements and innuendos which suggest false things without actually saying so.

sections.label: US Capitol attack example
sections.summary: The US Capitol attack on 6 January 2021 is cited as perhaps the most shocking example.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the most shocking example of this was the US Capitol attack on 6 January 2021.

sections.label: Unity, diversity and avoiding populism
sections.summary: People must be brought forward in unity even with diversity, and one more principle is added: do what is right and avoid populism.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We must always strive to bring people forward in unity, even with diversity.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I would add one more point to Mr Cheng's four principles, which is that we should consistently endeavour to do what is right and avoid a descent into populism.
